edits.old: In MongoDB's default viewful time-series implementation, the user-facing collection is a view over `system.buckets`, and queries unpack stored buckets into measurements. edits.old: MongoDB describes resharding as cloning collection data, building indexes, catching up pending writes, and committing a cutover. Its preparation guide calls for recipient-shard free space of at least 2 × (collection size + index size) divided by the destination shard count, a 24-hour oplog window, I/O below 50%, CPU below 80%, and tolerance for about two seconds of blocked writes. Treat resharding as a planned collection-wide workload. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Your application can tolerate a period of **two seconds** where the affected collection blocks writes.
